name: CAST
summary: A Sun-tracking axion telescope using a retired LHC test magnet and X-ray detectors, and an important technological precursor to IAXO.
detection_principle: Solar axions convert to X-rays through the inverse Primakoff effect in a Sun-pointing magnet bore, followed by focusing and low-background detection.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2024 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: A new upper limit on the axion-photon coupling with an extended CAST run with a Xe-based Micromegas detector

collaboration.name: CAST Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

phases.name: Vacuum and buffer-gas solar searches
phases.description: Different gas densities cover different mass intervals.

phases.name: Later low-background detector runs
phases.description: An extended dataset was published in 2024.

results.summary: Extended exposure found no signal; the 2024 analysis sets g_aγ < 5.8×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹ (95% CL).

science_scope: Primarily searches for solar-produced axions or hidden photons as complementary tests of dark-matter candidates. Solar flux is distinct from cold Galactic-halo dark matter; a solar-axion discovery alone would not establish the composition of cosmic dark matter.
